The Technology Governance Risk and Controls (GRC) function provides oversight of policy, standards, risks and controls across different areas. The function drives a better understanding of first line risks and will support, advise and facilitate the leadership team in actively managing risk by making decisions regarding the need for remedial actions and/or risk acceptances taking into account:

The current First Line GRC risk profile and control environment;
The relative scale of exposure and their likelihood; and
The cost and effort of remediating those exposures.

The policies and control frameworks managed by the team include Information Technology, Operational Resilience, Third Party Risk Management, Data and Privacy.

The primary role of the AVP is to perform control testing across Third Party Risk Management, Operational Resilience, Data & Privacy areas and support the development and improvements of the control framework across all areas managed by TGRC to ensure that it remains aligned to the M&G risk appetite. This includes, but is not limited to, understanding the external requirements (by regulators and industry bodies) and the organisation s strategy, vision and direction, external and internal emerging risk, and working closely with other leads in the function and wider M&G to understand the control framework and recommend improvements of policy, standards and control requirements. This will include overall assessment of the implementation of the control framework and will be supporting control owners to define corrective actions when gaps are identified. In addition, the role will support oversight of the Technology controls testing team and the issue assurance process providing validation of issue closure packs.

BASIC FUNCTION

jobDescription:
We re seeking an AI Engineer with strong hands-on experience in computer vision and multimodal (vision + voice) systems from data preparation and model training to scalable inference and production deployment. You ll build and ship end-to-end AI solutions: curate datasets, fine-tune and evaluate models, optimize inference pipelines, and operationalize services on cloud infrastructure.
Job Requirements
  • Bachelor s degree in Computer Engineering / Software Engineering / Electronics / Computer Science or equivalent (Master s preferred).
  • 0-3 years building production AI systems, with a focus on computer vision (PyTorch/TensorFlow).
  • Strong Python engineering skills; experience with REST/JSON APIs (FastAPI/Flask), and service design.
  • Hands-on with cloud deployment for AI (AWS/GCP/Azure), containers (Docker), orchestration (Kubernetes/Cloud Run/ECS), and GPUs.
  • Experience training and serving CV models (ResNet/EfficientNet, YOLO/RetinaNet, U-Net/nnU-Net, Vision Transformers), and familiarity with ASR/TTS pipelines (e.g., Whisper, torchaudio).
  • Practical knowledge of model optimization (ONNX/TensorRT, quantization), and data tooling (Pandas, NumPy, OpenCV, ffmpeg).
  • Proficiency with MLOps tooling: experiment tracking (MLflow/W&B), model registry, CI/CD, monitoring/logging (Prometheus/Grafana/Cloud Monitoring).
  • Strong grounding in evaluation methodology: metrics, ablation studies, error/bias analysis, and reproducible research practices.
  • Comfort with cloud storage, queues, and databases; experience integrating AI services into existing systems.
  • Computer vision: 2 years (Preferred)
  • Nice-to-Have:
    • Experience with multimodal (vision + workflows; Hugging Face ecosystem.
    • Knowledge of real-time/edge inference, TensorRT-LLM, vLLM.
    • Background in signal processing or audio engineering; speaker diarization, voice cloning ethics.
    • Experience in regulated domains with HITL workflows and documentation.
Main Job Duties
  • Model development and inference
    • Implement, fine-tune, and evaluate CV models (classification, detection, segmentation, tracking) using PyTorch/TensorFlow.
    • Build robust inference services (REST/JSON) with batching, streaming, and hardware acceleration (GPU, TensorRT/ONNX).
    • Train and adapt voice/ASR/TTS models and integrate with vision pipelines (multimodal workflows).
  • Data and evaluation
    • Own dataset lifecycle: collection, cleaning, labeling/specs, augmentation, and versioning.
    • Define metrics and test sets; run offline/online evaluations (accuracy, latency, throughput, calibration) and error analysis.
    • Develop data transformation and feature pipelines; maintain data quality checks and bias/fairness assessments.
  • Production engineering
    • Containerize and deploy models to cloud (AWS/GCP/Azure) using Docker/Kubernetes/Cloud Run/ECS.
    • Implement CI/CD, experiment tracking, model registry, A/B canaries, rollout/rollback strategies.
    • Build monitoring for drift, performance, and cost; automate retraining or active learning loops.
  • Systems integration
    • Design APIs and modules, integrate with upstream/downstream systems, and ensure reliable contracts and observability.
    • Collaborate with product, design, and backend teams to turn requirements into measurable deliverables.
  • Performance and optimization
    • Optimize training/inference (quantization, pruning, distillation, mixed precision); leverage ONNX/TensorRT/torch.compile.
    • Profile and tune data loaders, GPU utilization, caching, and I/O.
  • Compliance and safety
    • Implement data governance, privacy, and security best practices; maintain audit trails and documentation.
    • Establish HITL workflows and guardrails for clinical or safety-critical contexts where applicable.

title: Lead Applied AI / LLM Engineer
jobDescription:
Lead Applied AI / LLM Engineer

PERMANENT FULL-TIME OPPORTUNITY


RAG, Agents & Evaluation | Remote-first within India | Reports to the CTO

Joining: ASAP; within 30 days preferred
Fixed salary: INR 24,00,00028,00,000 p.a.

Location: Anywhere in India; Gurugram/NCR attendance as required
Work model: Flexible hours; core overlap 11:00 AM4:00 PM IST




The mandate:



AKS is building a permanent technical core of engineers who own outcomes, not isolated tickets. You will take end-to-end responsibility for applied AI systems across discovery, architecture, implementation, evaluation, deployment, UAT, production support, documentation and handover. You will coordinate directly with the CTO, collaborate with the full-stack lead and, where appropriate, guide interns or junior engineers while retaining accountability for the final result.


This is primarily an applied LLM and application-engineering role. Model training and research are part of the toolkit, but the central objective is to deliver reliable systems that work with real client data, constraints and acceptance criteria. A typical portfolio may include one or two active PoC/UAT builds and several systems in hypercare or maintenance.



What makes this role different:


AI coding agents and approved model/tool subscriptions are provided and encouraged. You remain accountable for architecture, correctness, security, tests and every accepted change. You must understand and be able to defend the system without relying on the tool that generated a suggestion.


What you will own

  • Convert ambiguous business and client problems into written technical outcomes, acceptance criteria and delivery plans.
  • Design, build and maintain production-oriented RAG, agentic and document-intelligence systems with explicit boundaries between deterministic logic, conventional ML and generative components.
  • Own ingestion, retrieval, embeddings, vector search, prompting, structured outputs, tool use, orchestration, guardrails and human-review paths.
  • Build defensible evaluations for retrieval quality, groundedness, citations, entity isolation, refusal behaviour, latency, cost and failure cases; turn production failures into regression tests.
  • Fine-tune models using LoRA or related parameter-efficient methods and deploy reproducible inference-serving workflows.
  • Develop production-quality Python services and APIs; integrate AI components with FastAPI applications, PostgreSQL/vector stores and frontend or workflow systems.
  • Deploy and troubleshoot services on cloud and client-controlled Linux/GPU environments using Docker, CI/CD, logging and monitoring.
  • Reuse proven components across applications without creating hidden coupling; improve existing repositories rather than rebuilding everything by default.
  • Maintain clear Git history, pull requests, tests, runbooks, architecture decisions, model/evaluation records and knowledge-transfer material.
  • Communicate progress, dependencies, risks and production incidents clearly to the CTO, delivery stakeholders and clients where required.
  • Review work and nurture interns or junior engineers when assigned; ownership cannot be delegated away.


Required capabilities

  • 3–7 years of relevant software, ML or applied-AI experience, including personally shipped systems.
  • Strong Python engineering and hands-on PyTorch proficiency.
  • Strong foundations in statistics, statistical machine learning, deep learning, experimental design and practical model evaluation.
  • Production experience with LLM applications, RAG or agentic workflows; ability to diagnose retrieval, grounding, hallucination, identity and tool-use failures.
  • Hands-on LoRA fine-tuning and inference serving, including data preparation, baselines, leakage control, versioning, evaluation, capacity and rollback considerations.
  • Working knowledge of embeddings, vector databases, information retrieval, structured extraction and document-processing pipelines.
  • Strong Git and GitHub proficiency: branches, pull requests, reviewable commits, code review and repository hygiene.
  • Strong Linux, Docker, REST API, testing and debugging skills; working knowledge of CI/CD, monitoring and at least one cloud platform.
  • Ability to reason about security, privacy, client-data boundaries, model/provider selection, cost, latency and production fallback behaviour.
  • Clear written and verbal communication; direct client discovery or review experience is highly valued.
  • Bachelor’s degree in Computer Science, AI/ML, Data Science, Statistics, Mathematics, Engineering or another relevant quantitative discipline.


Preferred experience

  • Quantization, GPU-memory/performance optimization, vLLM or comparable model-serving frameworks.
  • PostgreSQL with pgvector or other vector stores; Pydantic/FastAPI; evaluation and observability tooling such as MLflow, Langfuse, Phoenix or OpenTelemetry.
  • Enterprise document intelligence, legal/research assistants, RFQ/quotation automation, voice/calling automation or other high-trust workflows.
  • Local/on-premise model deployment, distributed inference, Kubernetes or infrastructure-as-code.
  • Conventional ML problems such as classification, forecasting or ranking where labels, calibration and business-valid metrics matter.
  • Informal technical leadership, code review and guidance of interns/junior engineers.


Success in the first 90 days

  • Establish a verified architecture, data-flow, evaluation and deployment map for the assigned portfolio.
  • Reproduce existing baselines and known failures; resolve at least one bounded maintenance issue through a reviewed deployment.
  • Put representative evaluation/regression checks into the delivery workflow and ship one measurable reliability improvement.
  • Demonstrate a reproducible LoRA training and serving workflow in staging.
  • Lead one active PoC/UAT workstream while maintaining transparent status and risk control across 4–5 systems.
  • Deliver or materially advance one system to a written acceptance milestone and leave reusable, documented components behind.

Work model and support expectations

  • Permanent, full-time and remote-first within India. Attendance at the Gurugram office or client meetings may be required with reasonable notice.
  • Eight working hours on each scheduled workday, excluding breaks. The normal reference window is 9:30 AM–6:30 PM IST with a one-hour meal break; start/end times may flex while preserving mandatory availability from 11:00 AM–4:00 PM IST.
  • Regular Monday–Friday schedule plus two pre-notified working Saturdays per calendar month. The Saturday schedule is communicated before the month begins.
  • Routine overnight support is not expected. Exceptional production incidents may occasionally require availability outside normal hours, handled under company policy and applicable requirements.
  • Client travel is currently infrequent and primarily within NCR. Approved business travel outside NCR is reimbursed; other required travel arrangements are confirmed in advance.

Compensation and support

  • Annual fixed gross salary: INR 24,00,000–28,00,000.
  • Performance-linked variable pay: up to INR 3,00,000 per annum, assessed and payable quarterly against written, measurable outcomes. Variable pay is not guaranteed and may be prorated for eligible service.
  • Company-funded access to approved coding agents, model APIs and role-relevant software subscriptions.
  • Approved learning resources or certifications may be company-funded where relevant to delivery.
  • A company laptop/workstation may be provided based on role and information-security requirements.
  • Paid leave, holidays and statutory benefits in accordance with company policy and applicable law.

Selection process

  1. Structured initial evidence and logistics screen with HR.
  2. Technical architecture and ownership interview with the CTO.
  3. Role-relevant synthetic work sample; approved coding agents may be used with disclosure and verification.
  4. Final alignment and, where appropriate, consent-based reference or document verification.

jobDescription:

Colour grading of the species for quantifying freshness


Location: India / Remote

Experience: 5-8 Years
Domain: Fisheries | Aquaculture | Marine & Inland Fisheries
Open to Travel: Yes, as required


About the Role

Wisewit Solutions is looking for a Fisheries Research Analyst AI & Computer Vision to bridge the gap between fisheries domain expertise and AI technology.

The role will involve researching fisheries and aquaculture processes, understanding real-world field challenges, collecting and validating domain data, and working closely with AI/ML and Computer Vision teams to develop practical technology solutions.

The ideal candidate will have a strong understanding of fish/aquaculture species, farming, seafood processing plants, production lines, exports, and fisheries terminology, along with an interest in AI, data and emerging technologies.


Key Responsibilities

Fisheries Domain Research

  • Research Indian marine, inland fisheries and aquaculture practices.
  • Study fish and shrimp species, production processes, farming practices and harvesting operations.
  • Understand fish health, disease indicators, feed, water quality and environmental parameters.
  • Research fisheries value chains, landing centres, farms, processing units and field operations.
  • Identify operational challenges that can potentially be addressed using AI and automation.

AI & Computer Vision Research

  • You will work with AI/ML and Computer Vision teams to translate fisheries requirements into technical inputs.
  • Identify suitable use cases for image-based identification, classification, detection and monitoring.
  • Help define fish/species categories, attributes, visual characteristics and domain-specific classifications.
  • Assist in developing guidelines for image and video data collection.
  • Review and validate AI-generated outputs from a fisheries-domain perspective.
  • Identify false positives, false negatives and domain-specific errors in AI models.
  • Support creation and validation of datasets for Computer Vision and Machine Learning projects.

Data & Dataset Development

  • Collect fisheries-related data from research papers, government sources, field studies and industry sources.
  • Organise and clean structured and unstructured datasets.
  • Support image/video dataset creation and annotation activities.
  • Develop domain-specific taxonomies, labels, metadata and reference datasets.
  • Verify the accuracy and consistency of annotated data.
  • Maintain documentation and version-controlled research references.

Field Research & Validation

  • Conduct field visits to farms, hatcheries, fishing locations, landing centres and processing facilities.
  • Interact with fishermen, farmers, aquaculture professionals and other domain experts.
  • Document actual field processes and operational challenges.
  • Collect images, videos, observations and other relevant field data.
  • Validate whether AI solutions work effectively under real-world conditions.

Research & Documentation

  • Conduct literature reviews and analyse scientific publications.
  • Track developments in fisheries technology, AI applications and aquaculture.
  • Prepare research reports, use-case documents and domain briefs.
  • Create clear documentation for technical and non-technical stakeholders.
  • Present research findings to AI, engineering and business teams.

AI Use Cases You May Work On

Depending on the project, the role may contribute to areas such as:

  • Fish and shrimp species identification
  • Fish size/length estimation
  • Fish counting and biomass estimation
  • Fish quality assessment
  • Disease or abnormality detection
  • Aquaculture pond monitoring
  • Fish grading and sorting
  • Fish catch classification
  • Image/video-based fisheries monitoring
  • Farm productivity analysis
  • Fisheries supply-chain intelligence
  • Computer Vision-based inspection systems

Required Qualifications

  • Bachelors or Masters degree in Fisheries Science, Aquaculture, Marine Biology, Zoology, Aquatic Sciences or a related field.
  • 15 years of experience in fisheries, aquaculture, fisheries research, field research or a related domain.
  • Strong understanding of Indian fisheries/aquaculture practices.
  • Good research, analytical and documentation skills.
  • Strong Excel/Google Sheets skills.
  • Ability to interpret scientific papers, research reports and technical information.
  • Good communication skills and ability to work with multidisciplinary teams.

Good to Have

  • Exposure to AI/ML, Computer Vision or Data Science.
  • Experience with image/video data collection or annotation.
  • Knowledge of Python, SQL, Power BI or similar analytical tools.
  • Familiarity with GIS/geospatial data.
  • Experience working with fisheries datasets.
  • Knowledge of fish/shrimp species identification.
  • Experience conducting field surveys or stakeholder interviews.
  • Understanding of AI model evaluation or dataset validation.

Who Would Be a Good Fit?

We are looking for someone who can say:

I understand fisheries, I understand the problem in the field, and I can explain that problem clearly enough for an AI/engineering team to build a solution.”

You don’t need to be an AI engineer. However, you should be curious about AI and comfortable working closely with technical teams.


Key Skills

Fisheries Domain | Aquaculture | Research | Data Analysis | Field Research | Dataset Validation | Computer Vision | AI Use Cases | Documentation | Stakeholder Interaction


Travel

This role may require travel to aquaculture farms, fishing locations, landing centres, processing facilities, research institutions and client locations across India.

Candidates should be comfortable with travel as required by project requirements.

jobDescription:
About melyn

melyn is a Canadian advisory firm that helps First Nations communities secure government
funding. We work out which programs a community qualifies for, build the case, write and submit
the applications, deal with the funders, and support delivery once the money lands. Our work
funds community buildings, land use plans, forestry equipment, economic development strategies,
cultural gatherings, and youth programs. We also build melyn Brain, our own software platform
that communities use to manage this work.

melynEmpower is our funding side. It is a small, high output team and this is its next hire.

The role

You will own funding files end to end. That means finding the right programs for a community,
building the case, writing the application, getting it submitted correctly, handling the funder
afterwards, and keeping the whole pipeline of live applications on schedule.

Writing is the largest single part of this job, but it is not the whole job. You will also do
research and eligibility analysis, coordinate directly with community staff to gather what an
application needs, prepare our own scope and budget documents, follow up with government program
officers, and own the master deadline tracker for the entire portfolio. This is a consultant
role in a small team, so you will own files rather than tasks.

Working hours

Our team and clients are in Canada, roughly 11.5 to 12.5 hours behind India. Because this role
includes client and funder contact, we need real overlap. Core hours are approximately 8:00 PM to 4:00 AM IST.

Between November and March this shifts about an hour later. Most of your
day stays clear for focused research and writing. We are saying this upfront because it is a
real commitment and we would rather you self select than discover it in week two.

Who we work for

Our clients are sovereign First Nations governments. Every application carries a community's name
and their priorities, decided by them, not by us. We are in a support role and we hold a high
standard of accuracy and respect in everything we produce. You do not need prior knowledge of
Indigenous communities in Canada, and we will teach you the context properly. You do need
curiosity, humility, and care about getting it right.

Why join

- Your work directly decides whether a community gets funded. The feedback loop is real and it
is measured in buildings and programs that exist
- Real ownership from month one, including the full funding pipeline
- Small team, direct access. You will work with our VP daily, not through layers
- Unusual breadth. You will learn funding strategy, writing, client work, and government
relations at the same time, which is rare this early in a career
- Room to grow into a senior grant lead as the team expands
ROLES AND RESPONSIBILITIES


Funding research and strategy
- Research funding programs and work out what actually decides eligibility, not just what the
guidelines say on the surface
- Match programs to communities based on their priorities, corporate structure, and history
- Track intake windows, application deadlines, and first come programs across many funders
- Sequence a community's applications across fiscal years so they are not competing with
themselves or reapplying for something they already hold
- Analyse funding gaps: what a community qualifies for and has never accessed

Application development
- Draft complete applications from project briefs, research, and client conversations
- Write in the community's voice rather than a consulting house voice. Each application should
read as though the Nation wrote it, and should not sound like the last one you wrote
- Build budgets, workplans, and cash flow tables that reconcile: totals that add up,
contribution percentages that meet program rules, line items that match the narrative
- Complete funder application forms accurately, including complex fillable PDF forms
- Prepare supporting documents: project summaries, council resolutions, budget narratives,
cover letters, letters of support

Submission and funder liaison
- Assemble and check complete submission packages, then submit through the correct channel to
the correct regional office
- Follow up with program officers on status and keep a clear record of every exchange
- Respond to funder due diligence questions, clarification requests, and requests for revised
budgets, often on short timelines
- Track outcomes, and understand why a declined application was declined

Client coordination
- Work directly with community staff, economic development officers, directors of operations,
and finance leads to scope projects and gather what applications require
- Chase outstanding documents, quotes, resolutions, and approvals, persistently and politely. A
large share of deadline risk is information that has not arrived yet, and managing that is
part of the role
- Keep community contacts updated on where their applications stand

Commercial documents
- Prepare our own scope of work and budget breakdown documents for client engagements
- Support proposals and decks that set out funding options for a community

Pipeline ownership and quality
- Own the master pipeline and deadline tracker as the single source of truth. This is part of the
job, not an administrative extra, and it is the fastest way to learn the whole business
- Flag deadline and eligibility risk early and loudly
- Run a final quality pass against the program's own criteria before anything is submitted
- Review colleagues' applications on repeat program types
- Support batch work, where one program is applied for across many communities at once, each
application researched and written distinctly

Verification standard
- Verify every fact from a primary source: names, titles, signing authorities, registration
numbers, corporate structures, dollar figures. We do not guess and we do not invent, ever. An
application that misstates a community's own facts damages their credibility with a funder,
not just ours. This is the hardest standard we hold and the one we will not compromise on

PREFERRED CANDIDATE PROFILE

Experience

1 to 3 years in grant writing, proposal or bid work, management consulting, donor funded program
management, policy research, or government funding advisory.

What we are looking for

- Excellent written English. Clean structure, plain language, and the discipline to cut. If your
writing needs heavy editing, this role will frustrate us both
- The ability to adapt voice. Writing convincingly as someone else is a real skill and it
separates good candidates here from great ones
- Research rigour, and comfort reading long government guideline documents closely rather than
skimming them
- Numeric confidence: build a budget, check it, and notice when a total is wrong
- Comfort dealing directly with senior client staff, and comfort chasing people for what you
need without being pushy about it
- Deadline discipline across many parallel files, with no one chasing you
- Ownership instinct. In a team this size, a file with no owner does not move
- Precision with facts. You verify rather than assume

Backgrounds that transfer well

- Grant writing, fundraising, or donor proposals at an NGO, including CSR and FCRA funded
programs and proposals to institutional funders
- Bid, proposal, or RFP response teams at IT or professional services firms. Deadline driven,
compliance checked, submission critical work is close to this
- Management consulting or Big 4 associate work, especially with public sector or grant funded
clients
- Programme management in the development sector, where donor compliance and reporting mattered
- Policy or research analyst roles with heavy writing output and stakeholder contact
